title: Governance and Risk Management

header.html: 5.1 Explain the importance of governance, risk, and compliance artifacts; 5.2 Explain the impact of risk management processes on the security of the organization
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1Governance documents

Document Purpose Binding?
Policies High-level rules set by management: what must be done and why Mandatory
Standards Specific required measures to meet a policy: baselines, passwords, physical security, encryption, RFC-based protocol standards Mandatory
Procedures Step-by-step instructions: SOPs and runbooks Mandatory
Guidelines Recommendations: benchmarks, advisories, implementation guides, reference architecture Optional
Plans Business continuity and disaster recovery Operational

Common policies

BYOD (bring your own device), acceptable use policy (AUP), clean desk, information security, incident response, data classification and retention, access control, data disposal, vulnerability disclosure, privacy.

Exam tip

. Policy = why and what (mandatory, high level). Standard = what exactly (specific). Procedure = how (steps). Guideline = advice (optional). The AUP says what users may and may not do with company resources.

2Risk management process

Stage What happens Items
Risk identification Find risks Asset identification, stakeholder ownership
Risk assessment Rate them Scoring, categorization
Risk analysis Understand them Impact, likelihood or probability, owner, current mitigations, qualitative vs quantitative
Risk register A recorded list of risks Communication, reviews
Risk treatment Decide the response Transferring, accepting, avoiding, mitigating

Treatment Meaning Example
Transfer Shift the risk to a third party Cyber insurance, outsourcing
Accept Live with it (documented, approved) Low risk, cost of fix too high
Avoid Stop the activity Cancel a risky project
Mitigate Reduce likelihood or impact Patch, add controls
Exam tip

. Insurance = transfer. Residual risk is what remains after controls. The risk owner accepts residual risk; management sets the risk appetite (how much risk is acceptable).

3Business-level considerations

Term Meaning
Business impact analysis (BIA) Finds critical functions and the effect of losing them (sets RTO and RPO)
Risk appetite How much risk the organization is willing to take
Residual risk Risk left after treatment
Stakeholder involvement and management oversight Decisions are owned by the business
Regulatory and legal Laws may require specific controls

Quantitative risk formulas

Term Meaning Formula
SLE (single loss expectancy) Loss from one event Asset value × exposure factor
ARO (annualized rate of occurrence) How often per year Number of events per year
ALE (annualized loss expectancy) Expected yearly loss SLE × ARO

Example: an asset worth $100,000 with 50% exposure has an SLE of $50,000. If it happens twice a year (ARO 2), the ALE is $100,000. A control costing less than the ALE reduction is worthwhile.

Exam tip

. ALE = SLE × ARO. Qualitative analysis uses ratings (high, medium, low); quantitative uses numbers and money.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors buys cyber insurance to cover ransomware losses. Which risk treatment is this?

  • ATransfer
  • BAccept
  • CAvoid
  • DMitigate
Show the answer

Answer: A. Insurance shifts financial risk to a third party, which is transfer.

S2A server worth 80,000 would lose 25% of its value in one flood. What is the SLE?

  • A80,000
  • B100,000
  • C3,200
  • D20,000
Show the answer

Answer: D. SLE is the asset value times the exposure factor: 80,000 × 0.25 = 20,000.

S3Floods happen once every four years (ARO 0.25) and each costs 20,000. What is the ALE?

  • A80,000
  • B20,000
  • C5,000
  • D25,000
Show the answer

Answer: C. ALE is SLE times ARO: 20,000 × 0.25 = 5,000 per year.

S4Management writes a document that says all laptops must use full disk encryption. Which type of document is this?

  • AA guideline
  • BA runbook
  • CA benchmark
  • DA policy
Show the answer

Answer: D. A mandatory high-level rule from management is a policy, backed by standards and procedures.

S5After a patch and monitoring, a small risk remains that the owner agrees to live with. What is the remaining risk called?

  • AInherent risk
  • BTotal risk
  • CTransferred risk
  • DResidual risk
Show the answer

Answer: D. The risk left after controls is residual risk, which the risk owner may accept.

S6A company stops offering a service in a country because compliance is too costly. Which risk treatment is this?

  • ATransfer
  • BAccept
  • CMitigate
  • DAvoid
Show the answer

Answer: D. Ending the activity that creates the risk is avoidance.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Which governance document is optional advice?

Show the answer

A guideline.

R2What is the difference between a standard and a procedure?

Show the answer

A standard states specific requirements; a procedure gives the steps.

R3Name the four risk treatments.

Show the answer

Transfer, accept, avoid and mitigate.

R4What is the formula for ALE?

Show the answer

Single loss expectancy times annualized rate of occurrence.

R5What does a risk register contain?

Show the answer

A list of identified risks with their analysis, owners and status.

R6What does a business impact analysis find?

Show the answer

Critical business functions and the impact of losing them.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Documents policy (mandatory, why), standard (specific), procedure (steps: SOP, runbook), guideline (advice), plans (BC, DR)
Policies BYOD, AUP, clean desk, information security, incident response, classification and retention, access control, disposal, vulnerability disclosure, privacy
Risk steps identify, assess, analyze, register, treat
Treatments transfer (insurance), accept, avoid, mitigate; residual risk remains
Numbers SLE = asset value × exposure; ALE = SLE × ARO; qualitative vs quantitative; BIA; risk appetite
